title: Solo dev, open-world superpower sandbox in Unreal 5.8 built with Claude: 6 weeks, free Steam Playtest
author: Phabdev
selftext:
Hi! I'm a solo developer. Since early September I've been building Superpower Sandbox, an open-world superpower sandbox in Unreal Engine 5.8 (C++), with Claude as my main collaborator.

You fly over a city, charge your Qi, fight with kung fu and energy beams, throw people and objects around with telekinesis, and bring buildings down floor by floor. No forced story, just powers and physics.

**How I use Claude**

* The project started with OpenAI Codex for the first prototype, then moved to Claude, which has written almost all of the game since: mostly Fable 5.1 and Opus (5 and 5.5) for the hard parts, Sonnet 5 for smaller delegated tasks. About 490 of the 830 commits are co-authored by Claude. I direct the design, review every pull request and test the builds.
* Tooling I would never have written alone: packaging scripts, automated "soak" runs where a bot pilot flies a route to catch crashes, a crash-report collector, a session log that records hitches, Steam upload scripts.
* Debugging: it tracked down a GPU crash that only appeared after \~7 minutes (a material parameter collection being unloaded while cached draw commands still pointed at it) by running the same build with the fix on and off.
* Not magic: it needs clear acceptance criteria, it sometimes claims things it didn't verify, and anything visual still needs a human looking at the screen.

**Other tools**

* Unreal Engine 5.8, Visual Studio, Git with LFS, GitHub. OpenAI Codex for the early prototype; I also tried Gemini via Antigravity and dropped it.
* Third-party assets from Fab and Kenney (CC0), plus one CC BY model, credited in the game.
* Steam key art and capsules: generated with ChatGPT and edited by me. Trailer music: Suno. No AI-generated content is in the game itself, and the game uses no AI service.

**What's new / what's still rough** Version 0.5 added controller support with a power wheel and lock-on aiming, new menus, destructible city buildings that collapse floor by floor, and dust and debris sounds. Still rough: NPCs can get stuck, animations and audio are placeholders, and the in-game look is simple low-poly (the key art is much prettier than the game).

**Playtest (free)** Free Steam Playtest for Windows, no cost, nothing to buy. Press "Join the Playtest" on the Steam page and it's added to your library right away: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5330980/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5330980/)

I'd love feedback from people who build with Claude too, both on the game and on the workflow. Happy to answer questions about the setup.
